description: Table 5 is a single rendered data table comparing the formability of duplex Fe-Mn-Al-C steels with conventional DP steels. It has nine columns: Steel, Annealing treatment, Microstructure, UTS (MPa), TE (%), HEC^a (%), BA (°), DEH (mm) and ST (mm). Rows give: Fe-26Mn-9.7Al-0.47C [60] after 830 °C 1 min (γ + δ (21.8%); 945 MPa; 22%; 26%; 135°; 8.5 mm; 1 mm) and after 900 °C 1 min (γ + δ (28.3%); 882 MPa; 30%; 37%; 142°; 10 mm; 1 mm); Fe-22Mn-(7-11)Al-(0.7-1.0)C [5] after 850 °C 3 min (γ + δ (~7%); 974 MPa; 51%; 43%; 152°; 17.2 mm; 0.7 mm); Fe-25Mn-(9-13)Al-(0.9-1.3)C [5] after 850 °C 3 min (γ + δ (~5%) + κ; 999 MPa; 35%; 34%; 97°; 20.7 mm; 1.3 mm); and a reference range row DP500-DP1000, with no annealing entry, microstructure α + M (500-1000 MPa; 15-29%; 20-40%; 150-180°; 25-35 mm; 1 mm). The footnote defines HEC as Hole expansion capacity, BA as Bending angle, DEH as Dome expansion height and ST as Strip thickness. The table shows the Fe-Mn-Al-C variants reach comparable UTS and HEC to DP steels but generally lower BA and DEH, the lowest bending angle (97°) occurring for the κ-containing steel.

observations.observation: Table 5 has nine columns headed Steel, Annealing treatment, Microstructure, UTS (MPa), TE (%), HEC^a (%), BA (°), DEH (mm) and ST (mm), and five data rows.
For Fe-26Mn-9.7Al-0.47C [60] annealed at 830 °C 1 min the table lists microstructure γ + δ (21.8%), UTS 945 MPa, TE 22%, HEC 26%, BA 135°, DEH 8.5 mm, ST 1 mm.
For the same steel annealed at 900 °C 1 min the table lists γ + δ (28.3%), UTS 882 MPa, TE 30%, HEC 37%, BA 142°, DEH 10 mm, ST 1 mm.

Raising the annealing temperature of Fe-26Mn-9.7Al-0.47C from 830 to 900 °C increases the δ-ferrite fraction from 21.8% to 28.3% while UTS falls from 945 to 882 MPa and TE (22→30%), HEC (26→37%), BA (135→142°) and DEH (8.5→10 mm) all rise.
For Fe-22Mn-(7-11)Al-(0.7-1.0)C [5] annealed at 850 °C 3 min the table lists γ + δ (~7%), UTS 974 MPa, TE 51%, HEC 43%, BA 152°, DEH 17.2 mm, ST 0.7 mm.
For Fe-25Mn-(9-13)Al-(0.9-1.3)C [5] annealed at 850 °C 3 min the table lists γ + δ (~5%) + κ, UTS 999 MPa, TE 35%, HEC 34%, BA 97°, DEH 20.7 mm, ST 1.3 mm.
The Fe-25Mn-(9-13)Al-(0.9-1.3)C row has the highest UTS (999 MPa) and the lowest bending angle (97°) and lowest HEC (34%) of the three Fe-Mn-Al-C compositions.
The DP500-DP1000 row has an empty Annealing treatment cell, microstructure α + M, and property ranges UTS 500-1000 MPa, TE 15-29%, HEC 20-40%, BA 150-180°, DEH 25-35 mm, ST 1 mm.
The DP500-DP1000 comparison row shows the highest BA range (150-180°) and highest DEH range (25-35 mm) of any row, whereas its HEC range (20-40%) overlaps those of the duplex Fe-Mn-Al-C steels.
The caption defines the superscript a symbols as HEC: Hole expansion capacity; BA: Bending angle; DEH: Dome expansion height; ST: Strip thickness.
The caption states the table presents the formability of duplex Fe-Mn-Al-C steels in comparison with DP steels.
The citing text states the hole expansion ratio of Fe-Mn-Al-C steels is comparable with that of a DP600 steel.
The citing text states the bending angle and dome expansion height of Fe-Mn-Al-C steels are lower compared with conventional AHSS of similar strength levels.

The citing text suggests the low bending angle in duplex steels might be related to the formation and presence of δ-ferrite stringers within the γ-austenitic matrix, and notes ordered ferrite possesses brittle behaviour.

The citing text reports a strain hardening exponent of n = 0.58 measured for a Fe-28Mn-12Al-1C steel, higher than n = 0.33-0.45 reported for austenitic 304 stainless steel; this steel is not a row of Table 5.
